ai.description: This 30–40 cm snake is dark brown with irregular red lateral spots. It features a cylindrical body, a blunt, shield-like tail, and a small, pointed head. It belongs to the family Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis rubromaculata* is uniquely identified by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or red lateral stripe or series of spots along the body, unlike its plain kin.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis rubromaculata* inhabits the high-altitude montane shola forests and grasslands of the Nilgiri Hills in the Western Ghats, typically above 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Red-spotted Earth Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis rubromaculata* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis rubromaculata* is endemic to the high-elevation grasslands and forests of the Nilgiri and Anaimalai Hills in the Western Ghats (Tamil Nadu and Kerala).
